title: 2026-05-20 Polaris console economics & route telemetry walkthrough
summary: Intro + console walkthrough focused on per-route usage, cost attribution, and telemetry. Customer wants to understand how Redwood maps tokens to business routes, how to set budgets and alerts, and implications for dedicated vs hosted. Demo of route dashboards, token-level breakdown, trace linking to requests, and cost optimization suggestions. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with a telemetry export and a cost heatmap for top routes.

Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Polaris Head of Data), Samir Khan (Polaris CTO), Priya Mehta (Polaris SRE), Elliot Barnes (Polaris Product)

transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, joining me is Jonas our solutions engineer. quick intro round?
[00:08] Samir Khan: Hi Samir here CTO. we're mostly curious about how cost maps to our business lines, and what guardrails we can put in place.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Lena, head of data. we have dozens of 'routes' in prod and want per-route billing to chargeback to product owners.
[00:22] Jonas Reed: Great, we'll walk through the Console -- starting with per-route telemetry, token breakdown, and the cost attribution views. note the demo is on a sandbox dataset, not your prod.
[00:35] Elliot Barnes: quick Q — when you say route, is that like per-endpoint in our app or per-feature?
[00:40] Maya Patel: Good question. Route maps to the API route you configure in the SDK / proxy. you can group routes by product or feature tags for chargebacks.
[00:49] Priya Mehta: Do you require us to change anything in our infra to get per-route visibility?
[00:55] Jonas Reed: Minimal. you annotate requests with route id. we can also infer from path-based rules in the gateway. we'll show the mapping in the Console.
[01:05] [01:05] Jonas Reed: (screen share) Opening Console > Usage > Routes. top-left filter is time window. here we have a heatmap of traffic by route and a token histogram. you can see mean latency and p50/p95.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: hmm the token histogram — does that reflect prompt+completion tokens?
[01:24] Jonas Reed: yes combined. note: transcription sometimes labels it as "tokened" in older exports, but it's prompt+resp.
[01:35] Samir Khan: how do you calculate cost? is it per-token with model multipliers?
[01:40] Maya Patel: Cost model is per-token plus model weight. for hosted we show effective per-token cost broken down by model class, quantization, and batch. the Console shows total spend per route and also modeled marginal cost for incremental traffic.
[01:55] [01:55] Jonas Reed: (click) Here's a Route detail for "payments-invoice". you get a timeline of tokens, average completion length, and an estimated cost column. you can click "Explain" to see the components: model, batch size, KV cache hits.
[02:12] Priya Mehta: K V cache? we heard about K V cash yesterday (laughs) — can you explain?
[02:18] Jonas Reed: Sure — KV cache is key/value cache for autoregressive decoding; cache hit rates drastically reduce token compute. Console surfaces cache hit % per route (but in some older transcriptions it shows as K V cash or K V c-a-s-h, sorry).
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: Are there predicted savings if we enable more cache or batching?
[02:34] Jonas Reed: Yes the Optimize suggestions tab gives recommended batch sizes and cache pinning for high-traffic routes. it estimates savings and potential latency impact.
[02:44] [02:44] Maya Patel: Quick pause — do you have constraints like strict latency SLOs or cost ceilings per product?
[02:51] Samir Khan: We have p95 < 300ms for core billing flows and a monthly budget per product line.
[02:57] Maya Patel: Good, the Console supports alerts on p95 and budget burn rate. you can configure per-route SLAs and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if latency allows.
[03:08] Elliot Barnes: So can we auto-fallback to a smaller quantized model during bursts?
[03:13] Jonas Reed: yes, routing policies allow prioritized model sets — primary model, then quantized fallback. Console shows expected quality delta and rollback playbook.
[03:24] [03:24] Lena Ortiz: about data retention — we need route-level logs for audit for 12 months. Does Redwood retain full transcripts?
[03:31] Maya Patel: Hosted mode stores logs for configurable retention; enterprise/private deployments let you control retention in your VPC. we also have SOC 2 docs in the security pack. we'll share that.
[03:42] Priya Mehta: do you support KMS/HSM for keys?
[03:45] Jonas Reed: yes, KMS integrations and customer-managed keys are supported on Dedicated and Private. hosted offers envelope encryption with BYOK options.
[03:55] [03:55] Samir Khan: can we map costs to our internal accounting GL codes?
[03:59] Maya Patel: absolutely — the Console allows exporting cost breakdowns by route with tags. you can sync to your FinOps system via S3.
[04:07] Lena Ortiz: show us an example of the export?
[04:09] Jonas Reed: (click) Export > CSV. columns: route, model, tokens, percent cache, cost_estimate, owner_tag. we can push to your ledger or BigQuery.
[04:20] [04:20] Elliot Barnes: Any rough numbers for savings if we do route-level batching?
[04:24] Jonas Reed: Depends on distribution. for many customers we've seen 15-40% token cost reduction with smart batching+cache. if your traffic has many short prompts, batching helps.
[04:35] [04:35] Lena Ortiz: I'm worried about noise: if you group by route, will cross-routing requests be misattributed?
[04:41] Jonas Reed: We use request id and route tag heuristics. there is a "manual override" to reassign batches post-hoc in case of misattribution. we recommend a short pilot to validate attribution.
[04:52] Maya Patel: Let's pivot to alerts and budgets. (click) Here you can create a budget for route group "Consumer Payments" and set a burn-rate alert at 70% and an automatic throttle at 90%.
[05:05] Priya Mehta: throttle meaning reject or queue?
[05:08] Jonas Reed: You can choose throttle behaviors — reject with 429, degrade to cached response, or route to a cheaper model.
[05:16] [05:16] Samir Khan: latency when falling back — do you add overhead?
[05:20] Jonas Reed: small redirection overhead 10-20ms. if you fallback to a smaller model you might increase latency slightly but reduce compute cost. we surface those tradeoffs in the UI.
[05:32] Lena Ortiz: security question — are the trace links PII-safe?
[05:36] Maya Patel: Traces are tokenized; sensitive fields can be scrubbed at the SDK layer before sending. we also provide a filter to redact certain paths.
[05:45] [05:45] Elliot Barnes: competitor question — how does this compare to vertex's logging?
[05:49] Jonas Reed: Vertex provides logging but it's more infra-level; Redwood maps directly to product routes with chargeback-first UI and optimizer suggestions tuned to LLM patterns.
[05:59] Maya Patel: ok going to show the cost heatmap. (click) Heatmap ranks routes by spend and error rate. you can click into the top offenders and get recommended actions like batching, caching, or model swap.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: Can you create a saved view per team?
[06:15] Jonas Reed: Yep saved views and per-route dashboards can be shared with RBAC rules.
[06:20] [06:20] Priya Mehta: Do you allow synthetic traffic for testing? we want to run load tests without incurring real charges.
[06:26] Jonas Reed: We have a Test mode that flags synthetic traffic and excludes it from billing; good for bench.
[06:32] Samir Khan: About Dedicated vs Hosted — what triggers recommending dedicated?
[06:36] Maya Patel: Typically sustained throughput and strict performance/SLA needs. if you cross a certain token-per-second threshold and need guaranteed capacity or data residency, Dedicated or Private is recommended. we'll include a cost model in the pilot proposal.
[06:50] [06:50] Elliot Barnes: Any rate limits on the hosted tier?
[06:53] Jonas Reed: Hosted has quota controls per account. Dedicated provides predictable throughput via reserved GPU pools.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: let's talk about the pilot — what would you need from us to scope it?
[07:03] Maya Patel: sample route list, last 30 days token distributions, SLOs per route, and contact for infra/SRE. estimated 2-week pilot, we'll run telemetry export and build a recommended route config plus a cost heatmap and a short report.
[07:18] [07:18] Priya Mehta: we'll need an NDA and security pack before sharing logs.
[07:22] Maya Patel: understood — we'll send the security bundle and the NDA with the pilot proposal.
[07:28] Samir Khan: Any advocacy for model quantization? we worry about hallucination impact.
[07:33] Jonas Reed: Quantization reduces compute cost; the Console's Optimize tab simulates quality deltas with a test prompt set. you can schedule evals to ensure no regression.
[07:45] [07:45] Maya Patel: Quick demo of the Optimize suggestions — (click) shows top three route candidates for batching, expected savings, and a projected latency impact. you can export suggested config to your repo as YAML.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: how automated is rollout? can we do canary policies?
[08:02] Jonas Reed: Yes canary and A/B rollouts are supported in the Console: gradual traffic shifting, auto-rollback on quality regressions.
[08:12] [08:12] Elliot Barnes: Do you integrate with Sentry or our observability stack?
[08:16] Jonas Reed: We integrate with Datadog, Sentry, and Splunk via event export. traces include a Redwood trace id.
[08:25] Priya Mehta: If we go Private, how do updates work?
[08:28] Maya Patel: Private deployments get a controlled update cadence with tooling to stage rollouts; you'll have a private control plane and your infra team keeps access.
[08:36] [08:36] Samir Khan: cost — ballpark hosted unit price for standard LLM?
[08:40] Maya Patel: We'll send detailed pricing, but rough hosted effective per-k token ranges vary by model. for pilot we'll model expected spend and show cost-per-route.
[08:50] Lena Ortiz: ok let's finalize next steps.
[08:53] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to send pilot proposal + security pack by Friday (2026-05-22). Polaris to share sample routes and token volumes by Monday (2026-05-25). Pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-26. action items will be captured.
[09:09] Samir Khan: sounds good. thanks for the walkthrough.
[09:12] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email.
[09:15] [End of recording]
notes: Demo used sandbox dataset; customer requested NDA + security pack. Pilot scoped for 2 weeks to validate attribution and produce cost heatmap for top 15 routes.
